taxonomy.subtopic: Hepatic first-pass metabolism and serotonin-mediated right-sided fibrosis

questions.stem_html:
A 58-year-old woman has episodic flushing, watery diarrhea, wheezing, and a new systolic murmur that increases with inspiration. CT shows a small ileal neuroendocrine tumor and multiple liver lesions. Urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid is elevated. Review of older imaging shows that the intestinal tumor was present for years before systemic symptoms appeared.

Why did the syndrome most likely become clinically apparent only after liver involvement developed?

options.text_html: The primary tumor acquired a new ability to synthesize catecholamines
Portal hypertension redirected pancreatic enzymes into the systemic circulation
Bile-acid malabsorption activated enterochromaffin cells throughout the colon
The liver lesions destroyed monoamine oxidase in the lungs
Metastatic tumor bypassed hepatic first-pass metabolism of serotonin and other vasoactive products

questions.explanation_html: Products from a gastrointestinal neuroendocrine tumor usually enter portal blood and are metabolized by the liver. Hepatic metastases release them directly into systemic veins, enabling flushing, secretory diarrhea, bronchospasm, and right-sided endocardial fibrosis. Liver metastases allow serotonin and other mediators to reach the systemic circulation without effective first-pass hepatic inactivation.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Carcinoid syndrome is primarily mediated by serotonin and related peptides, not a required switch to catecholamine synthesis.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Pancreatic enzymes do not produce the flushing, diarrhea, and right-sided valvular fibrosis of carcinoid syndrome.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Bile acids can cause diarrhea but do not explain the complete syndrome or right-sided valve disease.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Serotonin is chiefly metabolized during hepatic first pass before reaching the systemic circulation; lung monoamine oxidase is not the key gate.

questions.educational_objective: Connect the onset of carcinoid syndrome from a gastrointestinal primary to hepatic metastasis, loss of first-pass metabolism, and preferential right-sided valvular fibrosis.
